kanban.comment: Read the kanban header and its body. kanban.md#detection: No boundary is required after it. common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar.

patterns.comment: A diagram comment starts at `%%` where a unit starts in the statement context, on its own or after a header, shape, icon or data block, with or without whitespace; its value stops before LF, U+2028 or U+2029. Inline `%%` inside node text, a shape label or class text stays in that text. Padding stops before separator-led common comments, which own their following directive-looking text. Neither percent sign of the mark belongs to a directive. kanban.md#comments: Its mark is `%%`. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.

`:::`: enters the class context. A class starts with `:::`. It takes the nonempty rest of its line segment as `class-text`, whitespace included. line = node data-block* | icon-line | class-line; icon and class lines start after indentation. Indentation counts every whitespace character other than a line feed once. kanban.md#the-statement-context: A `node-text` is one or more characters other than `(`, `[`, line feed, `)`, `{`, `}`, and `@`, as many as possible. kanban.md#the-icon-and-class-contexts: An icon starts with `::icon(`, compared case-insensitively. kanban.md#grammar: The unit names are those defined above. kanban.md#units-and-contexts: Indentation counts every whitespace character other than a line feed once.

An icon starts with `::icon(`, compared case-insensitively. It has a nonempty `icon-text` of as many characters other than `)` as possible, followed by `)`. line = node data-block* | icon-line | class-line; icon and class lines start after indentation. Indentation counts every whitespace character other than a line feed once. The begin reads indentation and the icon opener; the end reads the closing parenthesis after icon text. kanban.md#the-icon-and-class-contexts: An icon starts with `::icon(`, compared case-insensitively. kanban.md#grammar: The unit names are those defined above. kanban.md#units-and-contexts: Indentation counts every whitespace character other than a line feed once.

patterns.comment: An opener: `-)`, `(-`, `))`, `)`, `((`, `{{`, `(`, or `[`, tried in this order. It is an `opener` unit and enters the shape context. rule 3: A closer: `))`, `)`, `]`, `}}`, `(-`, `-)`, `((`, or `(`, tried in this order. It is a `closer` unit and leaves the shape context. Rule 4: A `shape-text` is one or more characters other than `)`, `]`, `(`, and `}`, as many as possible. Strings start only at a unit start, right after the opener; shape text keeps quotes after its first character and has no HTML rule. kanban.md#the-statement-context: A `node-text` is one or more characters other than `(`, `[`, line feed, `)`, `{`, `}`, and `@`, as many as possible. kanban.md#the-shape-context: A `string` runs from a quote to the next quote.
A quote and backtick start a markdown string, closed by backtick and quote. kanban.md#the-shape-context: A `string` runs from a quote to the next quote.
A double quote starts a string ending at the next double quote, without escapes. kanban.md#the-shape-context: A `string` runs from a quote to the next quote.
Read node text before a shape as the element name; bare nodes remain labels. kanban.md#nodes-and-shapes: A node is bare node text, node text followed by a shape, or a shape alone.
Read a bare node's text as its displayed label, stopping before a shape or data suffix. kanban.md#nodes-and-shapes: A node is bare node text, node text followed by a shape, or a shape alone.

kanban-shape-text.comment: Shape text takes as many characters other than ), ], (, and } as possible; quotes after its first character and percent pairs are text. Directives inside this text join its parts. kanban.md#the-shape-context: A `string` runs from a quote to the next quote.

kanban-data-block.comment: At a statement-context unit start, "@{" enters the data context, and the first "}" outside double quotes leaves it. Double quotes enter and leave quoted data; its content may hold braces, carets, line feeds and backslashes, with no escape rule. Single quotes are ordinary content and do not protect a caret or closing brace. Each data block keeps its whole written interior and has no parsed key/value children. kanban.md#the-data-context: A backslash does not escape the closing quote. kanban.md#data-blocks: It has no parsed key/value children.
